subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Prove that the area of the triangle formed by the tangents at (x₁,y₁), (x₂,y₂), (x₃,y₃) to the parabola y² = 4ax is (1/16a)|(y₁−y₂)(y₂−y₃)(y₃−y₁)| square units.

Set up the area determinant and factor it
Convert to y-differences and write the boxed area

steps.why: Every tangent to y² = 4ax at parameter t has the same shape ty = x + at², so subtracting two such equations cancels x immediately and gives y directly, which is the fastest way to the two tangents' meeting point.
common_mistakes: Using the point form of the tangent (yy₁=2a(x+x₁)) instead of the parameter form, which makes the elimination far harder.
Mixing up which pair of tangents meets at which of P, Q, R.
steps.memory_tip: The tangent at parameter t is always ty = x + at² — subtract two of these and x cancels, handing over y first.

steps.margin_note: Two marks. Half of this determinant's work was already done when P, Q, R were written down in step 1.

steps.why: Each coordinate difference of P, Q, R factors neatly because P, Q, R were themselves built from t₁, t₂, t₃ — substituting those factored forms into the determinant leaves one common factor (t₁−t₃)(t₂−t₃) that can be pulled straight out.
common_mistakes: Re-deriving X₁−X₂ etc. from scratch by expanding the coordinates instead of factoring them directly.
Losing the sign in the final factoring, which flips (t₂−t₁) to (t₁−t₂).
steps.memory_tip: P, Q, R were built from products and sums of t₁, t₂, t₃ — their differences factor the same way column by column.

steps.why: This area comes out to exactly half the area of the triangle formed by the three points of contact, for the same three parameters. Both proofs start from ½|determinant|, but here the y-differences of P, Q, R carry a (not 2a), so the determinant is a²(…) instead of 2a²(…) — that is why the denominator here is 16a instead of 8a.
common_mistakes: Reusing the points-of-contact triangle's final denominator of 8a instead of 16a — the determinant here is a²(…), not 2a²(…).

steps.memory_tip: This triangle (from tangents) is always half the area of the triangle formed by the points of contact themselves, for the same three parameters — 16a instead of 8a.

insider_note: This proof shares almost every line with the companion result for the triangle formed by the three points of contact themselves — here the determinant is a²(…) instead of 2a²(…), because the vertices' y-differences carry a, not 2a, which is exactly why the denominator here is 16a and not 8a.
